# google_document_ai_schema_version

SchemaVersion is a version of the processor's schema which is created as a child resource of Schema.


To get more information about SchemaVersion, see:
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/overview)

## Example Usage - Documentai Schemaversion


```hcl
resource "google_document_ai_schema_version" "schema_version_id" {
  display_name = "schema_version"
  location     = "us"
  labels = {
    "label" = "key",
    "foo" = "bar",
  }
  schema {
    description     = "schema_description"
    display_name    = "schema_description"
    document_prompt = "document_prompt"
    entity_types {
      base_types   = ["document"]
      display_name = "entity_display_name"
      properties {
        display_name    = "property_display_name"
        method          = "EXTRACT"
        name            = "name"
        occurrence_type = "MULTIPLE_ONCE"
        value_type      = "string"
      }
    }
  }
  schema_id = "schema_id"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The user-defined name of the SchemaVersion.

* `schema` -
  (Required)
  The schema defines the output of the processed document by a processor.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema).

* `location` -
  (Required)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.

* `schema_id` -
  (Required)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.


* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The GCP labels for the SchemaVersion.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.



<a name="nested_schema"></a>The `schema` block supports:

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Description of the schema.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Display name to show to users.

* `entity_types` -
  (Optional)
  Entity types of the schema.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types).

* `metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Metadata for global schema behavior.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_metadata).

* `document_prompt` -
  (Optional)
  Document level prompt provided by the user. This custom text is injected
  into the AI model's prompt to provide extra, document-wide guidance for
  processing.


<a name="nested_schema_entity_types"></a>The `entity_types` block supports:

* `base_types` -
  (Optional)
  The entity type that this type is derived from.  For now, one and only
  one should be set.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User defined name for the type.

* `enum_values` -
  (Optional)
  Defines the a list of enum values.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types_enum_values).

* `name` -
  (Optional)
  Name of the type. It must be unique within the schema file and
  cannot be a "Common Type".  The following naming conventions are used:
  - Use `snake_casing`.
  - Name matching is case-sensitive.
  - Maximum 64 characters.
  - Must start with a letter.
  - Allowed characters: ASCII letters `[a-z0-9_-]`.  (For backward
  compatibility internal infrastructure and tooling can handle any ascii
  character.)
  - The `/` is sometimes used to denote a property of a type.  For example
  `line_item/amount`.  This convention is deprecated, but will still be
  honored for backward compatibility.

* `properties` -
  (Optional)
  Description the nested structure, or composition of an entity.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types_properties).


<a name="nested_schema_entity_types_enum_values"></a>The `enum_values` block supports:

* `values` -
  (Optional)
  The individual values that this enum values type can include.

<a name="nested_schema_entity_types_properties"></a>The `properties` block supports:

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User defined name for the property.

* `method` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies how the entity's value is obtained.
  Possible values are: `EXTRACT`, `DERIVE`.

* `name` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the property.  Follows the same guidelines as the
  EntityType name.

* `occurrence_type` -
  (Optional)
  Occurrence type limits the number of instances an entity type appears
  in the document.
  Possible values are: `OPTIONAL_ONCE`, `OPTIONAL_MULTIPLE`, `REQUIRED_ONCE`, `REQUIRED_MULTIPLE`.

* `value_type` -
  (Optional)
  A reference to the value type of the property.  This type is subject
  to the same conventions as the `Entity.base_types` field.

<a name="nested_schema_metadata"></a>The `metadata` block supports:

* `document_allow_multiple_labels` -
  (Optional)
  If true, on a given page, there can be multiple `document` annotations
  covering it.

* `document_splitter` -
  (Optional)
  If true, a `document` entity type can be applied to subdocument
  (splitting). Otherwise, it can only be applied to the entire document
  (classification).

* `prefixed_naming_on_properties` -
  (Optional)
  If set, all the nested entities must be prefixed with the parents.

* `skip_naming_validation` -
  (Optional)
  If set, we will skip the naming format validation in the schema. So the
  string values in `DocumentSchema.EntityType.name` and
  `DocumentSchema.EntityType.Property.name` will not be checked.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}`

* `create_time` -
  The time when the SchemaVersion was created.

* `name` -
  Identifier. The resource name of the SchemaVersion.
  Format:
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/schemas/{schema}/schemaVersions/{schemaversion}`

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


SchemaVersion can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}`
* `{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}`


In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import SchemaVersion using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}"
  to = google_document_ai_schema_version.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), SchemaVersion can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default {{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}
```
